newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices seen strengthening in week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices seen strengthening in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to continue to strengthen at auctions in Sydney and Melbourne this week, with about 56,600 bales on offer, Wesfarmers Dalgety said in its weekly market preview.
"Demand is being driven by the threat of declining quantities for sale over the next month. Until mid-May, there is an average of only 53,000 bales for sale per week", Wesfarmers said.
Last week's auction prices reached the highest level in over 18 months. The eastern market indicator rose 14 cents to 640 cents a kg clean and the western indicator rose nine to 602.
The Australian Council of Wool Exporters noted Wool International sold 25,000 bales of stockpile wool last week.

At this level of clearances, the fact that auction offerings for the next three weeks are currently rostered in the 50,000 to 57,000 bales range each week is certainly adding considerable upward pressure on prices, particularly with the finer, better style types which have led the recovery in prices, it said.
These types are expected to be in increasingly shorter supply, it said.
